target_customer: Hobbyist and professional music producers who trade samples and loops with collaborators
problem: Producers share sound samples through ad hoc file transfers and chat apps, which is slow and breaks the flow of making music with others.
business_model: Freemium desktop app for sample sharing, with paid tiers implied by the free-to-start pitch (pricing not verified)
product_category: Music collaboration and sample sharing app

founders.name: Jack Damon
prior_employers: Viam (after Supertone, data and machine learning)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as a founder now working on data and machine learning at Viam. No education listed.

founders.name: Matt Cunningham
founders.background_notes: YC page gives no other details.

founders.name: Oliver Hill
previous_startups: Clearspace (co-founder and CTO, listed on YC page)
founders.background_notes: Listed as a founder on the YC page; role at Supertone not stated.

exit.reason: Cause not public. YC lists the company as Inactive.

technical_complexity.rationale: A desktop app with a feed and drag and drop into DAWs such as Ableton and Logic is mostly standard app engineering plus file sync, per the product site.

defensibility.rationale: File sharing between producers has no data or regulatory moat, and value depends on network density that a three person team had not built.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: CB Insights lists Splice as a competitor, and Splice launched its CoSo app in May 2022. No source shows Splice acting against Supertone specifically.

market_need_then: Producers already traded samples through chat and cloud drives, and Splice had built a large sample marketplace, which suggests demand for sample workflows. No source quantifies demand for a dedicated sharing feed.

branding.domain_note: Company uses supertone.com (exact .com). A separate, better known company, Supertone Inc owned by Hybe, shares the name, which hurts search clarity.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain product copy about sharing samples in less than 3 clicks and focusing on making music

brand_strength.rationale: No press, community or brand material found beyond directory listings, and search results are dominated by the unrelated Hybe owned Supertone.

outcome_analysis: Supertone joined YC in Winter 2022 with a three person team and an app still labeled beta. YC now lists it as Inactive, but no post-mortem, shutdown notice or press coverage was found, so the cause of failure is not public. The only funding evidence is a single database entry for a YC convertible note, and the website footer still reads 2021.
notes: The $500K figure rests on a single database (CB Insights). StartupHub's $13M and Village's $3.6M refer to a different Supertone (the AI voice company) and are ignored. Competitor Splice appears only on a CB Insights page with no date, so the list is empty. Outcome search found no shutdown article.
